nodes.description:
NDUFA12 is one of the roughly thirty supernumerary subunits acquired evolutionarily alongside complex I's fourteen conserved core subunits. Knockdown of NDUFA12 alongside NDUFA3 and NDUFA5 shows it is needed for a functional holoenzyme, and analysis of assembly intermediates places the requirement at assembly or stability of the electron-transferring Q module in the peripheral arm.
The complication is that patient cells lacking NDUFA12 entirely still contain fully assembled, enzymatically active complex I - in reduced amounts. That is why the founding study places NDUFA12 at a late assembly step or in stability rather than treating it as structurally indispensable, and it is a weaker requirement than the knockdown work implies. The two are not fully reconciled.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating NDUFA12 variants abolish the protein. The founding allele c.178C>T (p.Arg60X) introduces a premature stop codon, and western blot shows complete absence of NDUFA12 in patient fibroblasts. Functional complementation restores complex I activity, establishing the variant as causal rather than merely associated.

nodes.description:
NDUFA12's paralogue NDUFAF2 is a complex I assembly factor, and in NDUFA12-mutant patient cells it associates with the *active* complex. That behaviour is specific: in patient fibroblasts mutated in other complex I subunits, NDUFAF2 is instead attached to an inactive subcomplex (NDUFS1, NDUFV1) or not detected at all (NDUFS7). The paralogue appears to take the place of the missing subunit on an assembled, working enzyme - which is the most economical explanation for why complex I still functions without NDUFA12.
The relationship is directional and not symmetric. Loss of NDUFS4 causes near-complete loss of NDUFA12, but loss of NDUFA12 does not reduce NDUFS4.

evidence.reference_title: NDUFS4 deletion triggers loss of NDUFA12 in Ndufs4(-/-) mice and Leigh syndrome patients: A stabilizing role for NDUFAF2.
evidence.snippet: In NDUFA12-mutated LS patient cells, NDUFA12 absence did not reduce NDUFS4 levels but triggered NDUFAF2 association to active CI.

evidence.reference_title: NDUFS4 deletion triggers loss of NDUFA12 in Ndufs4(-/-) mice and Leigh syndrome patients: A stabilizing role for NDUFAF2.

nodes.description: Selective vulnerability of the optic nerve and its retinal ganglion cells, which at the mild end of the spectrum is the only affected tissue, with unremarkable brain imaging. Curated as a node distinct from the basal ganglia because the two dissociate: the largest series reports patients with one, the other, or neither, all carrying homozygous truncating variants, and visual involvement can appear years after a purely motor presentation.

nodes.description: Isolated biochemical complex I deficiency in muscle and fibroblasts, with the rest of the respiratory chain intact. Isolated complex I deficiency is the most frequent biochemical signature among mitochondrial diseases and has more than eighty monogenic causes, so the biochemistry alone does not point to NDUFA12.
